p: is incomplete and is teaching like this:
one who wants another to eat with him, … and he urges him … and makes a vow with regard to him, … this … is
one who wants another to eat with him, and he urges him to do so and makes a vow with regard to him, this vow is
the entire year should stand up on Rosh HaShana and say:
Any vow that I take in the future should be void.
provided that he remembers at the time of the vow

w.8: and he urges him … and makes … with regard to him … this

p: provided that he does not remember at the time of the vow
With what are we dealing here?
but he did not know with regard to which … he made the stipulation,
but he did not know with regard to which vows he made the stipulation,
and now he makes a vow.
If he remembers at the time of the vow and says:
I am vowing in accordance with the initial intention, … his vow has no substance. … he did not say: … I am vowing in accordance with the initial intention,

I am vowing in accordance with the initial intention, when I stipulated that all vows should be void, his vow has no substance. However, if he did not say: I am vowing in accordance with the initial intention,
he has uprooted his stipulation and upheld his vow.
